The regulation gives no strap dimension.","anchors":{"top_center":[1342.9676342368648,0],"bottom_center":[1342.9676342368648,2950.87],"center":[1342.9676342368648,1475.435],"left_edge":[0,1475.435],"right_edge":[2685.9352684737296,1475.435],"epaulet_plain_right_center":[671.27,325.45],"epaulet_plain_left_center":[2014.67,325.45]},"landmarks":{"epaulet_plain_right":{"x":419.87,"y":196.9,"w":502.8,"h":257.1},"epaulet_plain_left":{"x":1763.27,"y":196.9,"w":502.8,"h":257.1}},"landmarks_note":"rects are {x,y,w,h} in user units (0.01 in)","overlay_of":"garment-blues-class-b-shirt-male","documented":["the shirt and blouse have epaulets for every member (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1 / 4.1.12.2)","shoulder cords are worn along the shoulder seam and, if the garment has an epaulet, underneath it (9.3, 9.4.1)","no grade goes on the strap itself: officers slip a gray or blue epaulet sleeve over it, NCOs and airmen wear chevrons or collar insignia"],"assumed":["strap size and shape (the traced base image does not draw it)","button size and position","topstitch inset"],"fit":{"method":"original","score":null},"grade":"accessory"}
